title: Is "Better Data" Better Than "Better Data Miners"? On the Benefits of Tuning SMOTE for Defect Prediction

edges.target: SMOTE (Chawla et al.)
edges.ref: [7] Chawla, Bowyer, Hall, Kegelmeyer. 2002. SMOTE: synthetic minority over-sampling technique. JAIR 16, 321-357.
edges.evidence: SMOTUNED outperformed both the original SMOTE [7] as well as state-of-the-art method [4]. ... the use of off-the-shelf SMOTE should be deprecated.

edges.target: MAHAKIL (Bennin et al.)
edges.ref: [4] Bennin, Keung, Phannachitta, Monden, Mensah. 2017. MAHAKIL: Diversity based Oversampling Approach ... Software Defect Prediction. IEEE TSE.
edges.evidence: there was no reproduction package available for MAHAKIL so we wrote our own version based on the description in that paper ... SMOTUNED generated larger and better results than MAHAKIL

edges.target: MAHAKIL results regenerated on Bennin's datasets
edges.ref: [4] Bennin, Keung, Phannachitta, Monden, Mensah. 2017. MAHAKIL ... IEEE TSE.
edges.evidence: We verified our implementation on their datasets, and achieved close to their values ± 0.1. The difference could be due to different random seed.

edges.target: Bennin et al. MAHAKIL evaluation datasets
edges.ref: [4] Bennin, Keung, Phannachitta, Monden, Mensah. 2017. MAHAKIL ... IEEE TSE.
edges.evidence: We verified our implementation on their datasets, and achieved close to their values ± 0.1.

edges.target: Ghotra et al. classifier ranking (RF best ... SVM worst)
edges.ref: [17] Ghotra, McIntosh, Hassan. 2015. Revisiting the impact of classification techniques on the performance of defect prediction models. ICSE.
edges.evidence: Using their work, we can select a range of classifiers for this study ranking from "best" to "worst" ... even our "best" learner (RF) fails over half the time.

edges.target: Prior classifier ranking studies (Lessmann, Hall, Tantithamthavorn, Menzies, Jiang, Fu, ...)
edges.ref: [13, 15-18, 21, 25-27, 29, 32, 33, 35, 40, 53, 62, 67] e.g. Lessmann et al. 2008 IEEE TSE 34(4); Tantithamthavorn et al. 2016 ICSE.
edges.evidence: The discovery of an important systematic error in many prior ranking studies, i.e., all of [13, 15-18, 21, 25-27, 29, 32, 33, 35, 40, 53, 62, 67].

edges.target: Scott-Knott ranking (Mittas & Angelis; Ghotra et al.)
edges.ref: [43] Mittas, Angelis. 2013. Ranking and clustering software cost estimation models through a multiple comparisons algorithm. IEEE TSE 39(4).
edges.evidence: For the significance test, we used the Scott-Knott procedure [17, 43]. This technique recursively bi-clusters a sorted set of numbers.

edges.target: A12 effect size (Arcuri & Briand)
edges.ref: [3] Arcuri, Briand. 2011. A practical guide for using statistical tests to assess randomized algorithms in software engineering. ICSE.
edges.evidence: our hypothesis test H was a conjunction of the A12 effect size test (endorsed by [3]) and nonparametric bootstrap sampling [12]

edges.target: Non-parametric bootstrap (Efron & Tibshirani)
edges.ref: [12] Efron, Tibshirani. 1994. An introduction to the bootstrap. Chapman and Hall, London.
edges.evidence: our Scott-Knott divided the data if both bootstrapping and an effect size test agreed that the division was statistically significant (99% confidence)

edges.target: CK object-oriented metrics (Chidamber & Kemerer)
edges.ref: [8] Chidamber, Kemerer. 1994. A metrics suite for object oriented design. IEEE TSE 20(6), 476-493.
edges.evidence: Table 1: OO CK code metrics used for all studies in this paper. ... These are all open source JAVA OO systems described in terms of the CK metrics.

edges.target: AUC / ROC curve (Duda et al.; Swets)
edges.ref: [60] Swets. 1988. Measuring the accuracy of diagnostic systems. Science 240(4857), 1285. / [11] Duda, Hart, Stork. Pattern classification.
edges.evidence: Area Under Curve (AUC), which is the area covered by an ROC curve [11, 60] in which the X-axis represents, false positive rate and the Y-axis represents true positive rate.

edges.target: Four evaluation criteria (recall, precision, false alarm, AUC) as widely reported
edges.ref: [16] Fu, Menzies, Shen. 2016. Tuning for software analytics: Is it really necessary? IST 76. / [17] Ghotra et al. 2015 ICSE.
edges.evidence: this paper evaluates the defect predictors using the four criteria mentioned above (since these are widely reported in the literature [16, 17]))

edges.target: Repeated k-fold cross-validation protocol (Refaeilzadeh et al.)
edges.ref: [56] Refaeilzadeh, Tang, Liu. 2009. Cross-validation. In Encyclopedia of database systems. Springer, 532-538.
edges.evidence: Our cross-validation study [56] is defined as follows: (1) We randomized the order of the data set D_i five times.

edges.target: Zhang's equation linking performance measures (Zhang & Zhang)
edges.ref: [70] Zhang, Zhang. 2007. Comments on Data Mining Static Code Attributes to Learn Defect Predictors. IEEE TSE 33(9), 635-637.
edges.evidence: known that our performance measures are inter-connected via the Zhang's equation [70]. Hence, increasing (e.g.,) recall might potentially have the adverse effect of driving up (e.g) the false alarm rate.

edges.target: Distance metrics in high dimensions: r < 1 (Aggarwal et al.)
edges.ref: [1] Aggarwal, Hinneburg, Keim. 2001. On the surprising behavior of distance metrics in high dimensional space. ICDT. Springer, 420-434.
edges.evidence: Aggarawal et al. [1] argue that with data being highly dimensional, r should shrink to some fraction less than one (hence the bound of r = 0.1 in Table 5).

edges.target: SEACRAFT defect data (jEdit, Camel, Tomcat, Ivy, Arcilook, Redaktor, Ant, Synapse, Velocity)
edges.ref: SEACRAFT repository http://tiny.cc/seacraft (no origin paper cited; prior users [24, 51, 52, 63])
edges.evidence: only imbalanced class data sets were selected from SEACRAFT (http://tiny.cc/seacraft). ... These data sets have used in various case studies by various researchers [24, 51, 52, 63]

edges.target: Scikit-learn (Pedregosa et al.)
edges.ref: [48] Pedregosa et al. 2011. Scikit-learn: Machine learning in Python. JMLR 12, 2825-2830.
edges.evidence: For implementations of these learners, we used the open source tool Scikit-Learn [48].

edges.target: Differential evolution (Storn & Price)
edges.ref: [59] Storn, Price. 1997. Differential evolution - a simple and efficient heuristic for global optimization over continuous spaces. J. Global Optimization 11(4).
edges.evidence: SMOTUNED uses DE (differential evolution [59]) to explore the parameter space of Table 5.

edges.target: DE competitive with PSO/GA (Vesterstrom & Thomsen)
edges.ref: [65] Vesterstrom, Thomsen. 2004. A comparative study of differential evolution, particle swarm optimization, and evolutionary algorithms ... CEC2004.
edges.evidence: Vesterstrom et al. [65] find DE's optimizations to be competitive with other optimizers like particle swarm optimization or genetic algorithms.

edges.target: Prior DE-based parameter tuning (Fu & Menzies; Agrawal et al.; Chiha; Omran)
edges.ref: [2] Agrawal, Fu, Menzies 2016 arXiv:1608.08176; [14] Fu, Menzies 2017 arXiv:1703.00133; [16] Fu, Menzies, Shen 2016 IST; [9]; [46]
edges.evidence: DEs have been used before for parameter tuning [2, 9, 14, 16, 46]) but this paper is the first attempt to do DE-based class re-balancing for SE data

edges.target: CK metrics used 49% vs McCabe 27% vs process 24% (Radjenovic et al.)
edges.ref: [53] Radjenovic, Hericko, Torkar, Zivkovic. 2013. Software fault prediction metrics: A systematic literature review. IST 55(8), 1397-1418.
edges.evidence: the CK metrics are used twice as much (49%) as more traditional source code metrics such as McCabes (27%) or process metrics (24%)

edges.target: SE data class imbalances 1:7 ... 1:249 (Menzies et al.)
edges.ref: [36] Menzies, Dekhtyar, Distefano, Greenwald. 2007. Problems with Precision: A Response to comments on data mining static code attributes. IEEE TSE 33(9).
edges.evidence: Menzies et al. [36] reported SE data sets often contain class imbalance. In their examples, they showed static code defect prediction data sets with class imbalances of 1:7; 1:9; 1:10; 1:13; 1:16; 1:249.

edges.target: Defect predictors learn in seconds (Fu, Menzies & Shen, Table 9)
edges.ref: [16] Fu, Menzies, Shen. 2016. Tuning for software analytics: Is it really necessary? IST 76, 135-146.
edges.evidence: it can be a matter of just a few seconds to learn a defect predictor (see the runtimes in Table 9 of reference [16]).

edges.target: Static bug finders vs defect predictors equally cost-effective (Rahman et al.)
edges.ref: [54] Rahman, Khatri, Barr, Devanbu. 2014. Comparing Static Bug Finders and Statistical Prediction. ICSE, 424-434.
edges.evidence: Rahman et al. [54], found no significant differences in the cost-effectiveness of (a) static code analysis tools FindBugs and Jlint, and (b) static code defect predictors.

edges.target: SMOTE value depends on the learner (Kamei et al.; Van Hulse et al.)
edges.ref: [28] Kamei, Monden, Matsumoto, Kakimoto, Matsumoto. 2007. The effects of over and under sampling on fault-prone module detection. ESEM. / [64] Van Hulse et al. 2007 ICML.
edges.evidence: They reported that SMOTE improved the prediction performance of the linear and logistic models, but not neural network and decision tree models.

edges.target: Hall et al. SLR: imbalanced data hurts C4.5
edges.ref: [21] Hall, Beecham, Bowes, Gray, Counsell. 2012. A systematic literature review on fault prediction performance in software engineering. IEEE TSE 38(6).
edges.evidence: Hall et al. [21] found that models based on C4.5 under-perform if they have imbalanced data while Naive Bayes and Logistic regression perform relatively better.

not_reuse_examples: [37] Menzies & Di Stefano 2004 blind-spot sampling: introductory motivation only, nothing adopted.
[38] Menzies et al. 2007 balance / G-measure: mentioned explicitly as criteria NOT used in this paper.
[5] Bird et al. 2009 socio-technical networks and [71] Zimmermann & Nagappan 2008: background survey of defect-prediction approaches, not used.
[66] Voas & Miller 1995 testability: background claim that quality costs exponentially more, not a premise of any experiment.
notes: ICSE'18 empirical paper (Agrawal & Menzies) proposing SMOTUNED (DE-tuned SMOTE); own re-implementation of MAHAKIL verified against Bennin's numbers; SEACRAFT data has no origin citation so dataset edge is transitive with self=true inferred from the repository's maintainers; 16-paper ranking-study group collapsed into one refutes edge.
